h: חַג הַפֶּסַח, מַאֲמָר ל״א Pesach — Maamar Lamed Aleph
Majesty and Splendor Is His Work: The Garments of Atika and the Dew of the Oral Torah

p: (כֵּן צָרִיךְ לִהְיוֹת, וְכֵן הוּא בִּדְפוּס חָדָשׁ)
(so it should read, and so it is in the new printing)
the intellect hidden from all thought.
Hashem has done greatly with these" —
And it is as we say:
"And in His goodness He renews every day, constantly,
for the world was created through words of Torah,
And afterward He renews every day
He renews every day the work of creation.
And after the Giving of the Torah,
נִמְסַר חִידּוּשׁ תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה לַחֲכָמִים,
the innovation of the Oral Torah was given over to the Sages,
for they engage in the building of the world
וְזֶהוּ הִגְדִּיל ה' לַעֲשׂוֹת עִם אֵלֶּה,
And this is "Hashem has done greatly with these":
that Hashem, may He be blessed, shines in the hearts of the Sages
טַל שֶׁבּוֹ עָתִיד לְהַחֲיוֹת אֶת הַמֵּתִים
the dew with which He will revive the dead
And this is "has done greatly," etc.
Majesty and splendor are the first garment
that Hashem, may He be blessed, put on
(דְּבָרִים רַבָּה ב', ל"ו, וּבְשִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה ד', כ"ב),
and they correspond to the ten sefiros.
it reckons the first garment as majesty and splendor;
and so it appears from the verse:
"Hashem my God, You are very great."
and "You are very great," without measure,
and it is written: "You have donned majesty and splendor,"
and afterward: "Wrapping Himself in light as a garment,"
which is the utterance "Let there be light,"
"From where was the light created?" etc.
"The Holy One, blessed be He, wrapped Himself
and His light shone forth," etc.
And the utterance "Let there be light"
the garment of majesty is Kesser.
And "splendor" — it is stated in the Gemara
"The splendor of the face is the beard,"
And this is what is said
and the hair of His head like clean wool" —
which is a crown upon the head.
And this is what is said
for he, peace be upon him, was the first
that there is an intellect hidden from all thought.
And this is what they said
"Until Avraham there was no old age"
And these two crowns, majesty and splendor,
were given to Israel at the Giving of the Torah.
And it is written: "Majesty and splendor is His work,"
for the deeds of the righteous are also written
in the name of the Holy One, blessed be He,
"The Sanctuary, Hashem, that Your hands established,"
as referring to the works of the hands of the righteous.
the works of the hands of the righteous —
And "His work" is the primordial light,
"And from where do we know that the reward of the righteous
which You have wrought (pa'alta) for those who trust.'"
And this is in the manner of what is written
"He took a seventh and placed it for them in its stead,
and the rest He hid away for the righteous" —
the revelation of the utterance "Let there be light," Chochmah.
corresponding to the five books of the Torah
"Your goodness" — "good means nothing other than Torah"
"Your great goodness that You have hidden"
the tip of the Yud alludes to Ayin
Atika, the most hidden of all hidden,
And on Shabbos is the revelation of Atika,
the head of Ze'ir Anpin is filled
from the dew that descends from Atika Kadisha," etc.,
And this is what they said in the Midrash
'Let Your work be seen by Your servants'" —
that is, they merit the hidden light
שֶׁל תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה, טַלָּא דְּעַתִּיקָא;
of the Oral Torah, the dew of Atika;
that they merit the crown of splendor.
And the Midrash skips the verse
"sought out by all who desire them,"
for all their desires are words of Torah,
that Torah scholars are like Shabbosos,
for they are always free for Torah.
"And let all your deeds be for the sake of Heaven";
that is, when the intent is for the sake of Heaven,
אָז כָּל חֶפְצֵיהֶם בִּכְלַל חֶפְצֵי שָׁמַיִם,
then all their desires are included in the desires of Heaven,
and they are words of Torah.
"He made a remembrance for His wonders":
And as at the Splitting of the Sea,
and akin to what is said
"As in the days of your going out of Egypt
וּמִזֶּה יֵשׁ רַק זֵכֶר בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה,
And of this there is only a remembrance in this world,
but the essence will be revealed on that day,
the attribute of Atika, which is called Hu
And it says in the Midrash:
for they merit the garment of majesty and splendor,
And likewise "Your righteousness is righteousness forever,"
when there is the union of Tzaddik and Tzedek,
and the union of the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah,
it is when there is the revelation of the union of Yud-Hei,
as brought in the holy Zohar
"The Cause of causes does not dwell there,
וּכְאִילּוּ לָא הֲוָה קוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא
and it is as if the Holy One, blessed be He, is not
וּכְשֶׁיֵּשׁ יִחוּד קוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא וּשְׁכִינְתֵּיהּ,
And when there is the union of the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah,
necessarily there is the union of Yud-Hei,
the Cause of causes, Kesser Elyon,
which is the entire Name Havayah.
And this is "Your righteousness is righteousness forever."
And this is revealed on Shabbos,
which is a semblance of the World to Come,
and its essence will be revealed in the World to Come:
"On that day Hashem will be One

paragraphs.text: Parallel: R. Avraham Yehoshua Heschel of Apta, Ohev Yisrael, Toldos — “The Midrash says there is no day on which the Holy One, blessed is He, does not renew a halachah in the heavenly court. We say, ‘And in His goodness He renews every day, constantly, the work of creation,’ and since the world was created through the Torah, the daily renewal of creation must also come through renewal in the Torah and the halachos that the righteous of every generation innovate each day. When they engage in Torah and mitzvos, Hashem pours upon them upright intellect and understanding to derive one thing from another and grasp the reasons of the Torah, and so they innovate new halachos every day, and through this the work of creation is renewed daily.” Connection: The Ohev Yisrael draws the same chain, Torah as the instrument of creation, the daily heavenly halachah, and the daily renewal of creation, and adds that it runs through the Sages' innovations as an intellect poured into them from above.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Bo 10 — “The Holy One was occupied in the days of action with creating the world through the Torah, and so He renews every day continually the work of creation. The renewal of creation each day is through the renewal of words of Torah each day. Before the Giving of the Torah Hashem was the One who renewed; once the Torah was given, ‘it is not in heaven,’ and He handed this to Israel. That is why Torah scholars are called ‘your builders’… who are occupied with building the world.” Connection: It makes the same move from Hashem’s daily renewal of creation through new halachah to the Sages after Sinai as ‘builders,’ and adds that this toil in Torah was man’s first calling, before toil for bread.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Chayei Sarah 1 — “In the Tanchuma it expounds ‘You have clothed Yourself in glory and majesty’: ‘With Your glory and majesty You clothed the head of Avraham,’ as it says, ‘And Avraham was old’; and in Midrash Rabbah: ‘You have taken up My craft; come and wear My garment.’ ‘Great’ indicates without measure, and ‘very great,’ without end… The Pesikta counts the first garment, ‘You have clothed Yourself in glory and majesty,’ against Keser Elyon, and then the second garment, ‘who wraps Himself in light,’ the saying ‘Let there be light,’ against Chochmah.” Connection: It sets out the same order of garments and Avraham’s old age, and adds its use for Sarah, whose garment was the clouds of glory.
